text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The European Commission decided to include Estonia in the first round of talks over European Union membership.
- A drug test on Estonian hurdler Tiia Eeskivi showed up positive last week. The Estonian Light Athletics Union proposes a two-year competition ban.

- The government approved plans for the privatisation of distilling plants. The shares of the Rakvere plant will be sold after negotiations, the sale of Liviko in several stages with 44 percent of stock sold in 1997 in open bids.
- A 100 kilometre per hour speed limit that came in force for an experimental month period is the highest limit in the northern countries. The traffic police are against the experiment.
All 12,000 tickets have been sold to a concert at the Lake Tamula in Voru on August 23 with Handel's Water Music and fireworks in the programme.
- Some customs tariffs on imported goods may be imposed, the economy and agriculture ministers said after a government session, rejecting warnings of ex-prime minister Tiit Vaehi against this step.
- The Unrepresented Nations Organisation will elect a new chairman and two vice chairmen today at an assembly in Otepaa.
- Estonian border guards detained a man who had delivered numerous bomb threats in Latvia.
- The Festival of Finno-Ugrian folk music will begin tomorrow in the southern town of Tartu with 240 performers representing all Finno-Ugrian peoples.
